verses.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by God's will, and our brother Timothy, to God's church in Corinth and all God's people throughout Achaia:
Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Praise the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of compassion and the God who comforts us in every way.
He comforts us in all our troubles so we can comfort others in any trouble with the comfort we ourselves receive from God.
Just as we share deeply in Christ's sufferings, we also receive abundant comfort through Christ.
If we go through trouble, it's for your comfort and salvation. If we're comforted, it's for your comfort too, helping you endure the same sufferings we face.
Our hope for you is firm, because we know that as you share in our sufferings, you also share in our comfort.
Brothers and sisters, we want you to know about the trouble we faced in Asia. We were weighed down far beyond our strength, so much that we gave up hope of staying alive.
We felt as if we had received a death sentence, so we wouldn't rely on ourselves but on God, who raises the dead.
He rescued us from such a deadly danger, and he will keep rescuing us. We've set our hope on him that he will rescue us again,
as you help us through your prayers. Then many people will give thanks for the blessing granted to us through the prayers of many.
Here's what we're proud of: our conscience confirms that we have lived in the world—and especially among you—with holiness and sincerity from God, not with human wisdom but with God's grace.
We're not writing anything beyond what you can read and understand. I hope you'll understand it fully,
just as you've partly understood us: that you can be proud of us, as we can be proud of you, on the day of our Lord Jesus.
Because I was confident about this, I planned to visit you first so you could receive a double blessing,
then travel through you to Macedonia, return from Macedonia to you, and have you send me on my way to Judea.
When I made those plans, was I being careless? Do I make plans like people who say ‘Yes, yes’ and ‘No, no’ at the same time?
As surely as God is faithful, our message to you wasn't both ‘Yes’ and ‘No.’
God's Son, Jesus Christ, whom Silvanus, Timothy, and I preached among you, wasn't ‘Yes’ and ‘No.’ In him it has always been ‘Yes.’
Every promise God has made is ‘Yes’ in Christ. That's why through him we say ‘Amen’ to God's glory.
God is the one who makes both us and you stand firm in Christ. He has anointed us,
put his seal on us, and given us the Spirit in our hearts as a guarantee.
I call God as my witness, and stake my life on this: I didn't come back to Corinth because I wanted to spare you.
We aren't trying to control your faith. We're working with you for your joy, because you stand firm through faith.
So I decided not to make another painful visit to you.
If I cause you pain, who can make me glad except the person I hurt?
I wrote as I did so that, when I came, I wouldn't be saddened by the very people who should make me glad. I was confident that all of you would share in my joy.
I wrote to you with many tears and much pain in my heart—not to make you sad, but to show you how deeply I love you.
If anyone has caused sorrow, they haven't hurt me so much as they've hurt all of you, though I don't want to overstate it.
The punishment given by most of you to that person is enough.
Now you should forgive and comfort them instead. Otherwise, they may be overwhelmed by too much sorrow.
So I urge you to reaffirm your love for them.
I wrote to you for this reason too: I wanted to see whether you would stand the test and obey in everything.
If you forgive anyone, I forgive them too. And whatever I have forgiven—if there was anything to forgive—I have forgiven for your sake in Christ's presence,
so that Satan can't get the upper hand over us. We know how his schemes work.
When I came to Troas to share Christ's Good News, the Lord opened a door for me.
But I had no peace of mind because I couldn't find my brother Titus. So I said goodbye to them and went on to Macedonia.
Thanks be to God, who always leads us in Christ's victory parade and spreads the knowledge of him through us everywhere like a sweet fragrance.
We are the fragrance of Christ to God among those being saved and those who are perishing.
To some, we are a smell that leads from death to death; to others, a fragrance that leads from life to life. Who is up to this task?
We aren't like so many people who peddle God's word for profit. Instead, in Christ we speak sincerely, as people sent by God and standing in God's presence.
Are we starting to recommend ourselves again? Do we need letters of recommendation to you or from you, like some people do?
You yourselves are our letter, written on our hearts and known and read by everyone.
It's clear that you are a letter from Christ, delivered through our service. It wasn't written with ink but with the Spirit of the living God—not on stone tablets, but on human hearts.
This is the confidence we have through Christ before God.
It's not that we're qualified on our own to claim anything as coming from us. Our qualification comes from God.
He has qualified us to serve a new covenant—not a written code, but the Spirit. The written code brings death, but the Spirit gives life.
If the ministry that brought death, carved in letters on stone, came with glory—so much so that the Israelites couldn't look steadily at Moses' face because of its fading glory—
won't the ministry of the Spirit come with even greater glory?
If the ministry that brought condemnation had glory, the ministry that brings righteousness has far greater glory.
In fact, what once had glory has lost its glory in comparison with the glory that surpasses it.
If what was fading came with glory, how much greater is the glory of what lasts!
Since we have this hope, we speak with great boldness.
We're not like Moses, who put a veil over his face so the Israelites wouldn't see the end of what was fading away.
But their minds were closed. To this day, that same veil remains when the old covenant is read; it hasn't been removed, because it is taken away only in Christ.
Even today, whenever Moses is read, a veil covers their hearts.
But whenever someone turns to the Lord, the veil is removed.
The Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.
All of us, with unveiled faces, reflect the Lord's glory and are being transformed into his image, from one degree of glory to another. This comes from the Lord, who is the Spirit.
Since God has shown us mercy and given us this ministry, we don't give up.
We've rejected secret, shameful ways. We don't act deceptively or twist God's word. Instead, we openly present the truth and commend ourselves to everyone's conscience before God.
If our Good News is hidden, it's hidden from those who are perishing.
The god of this age has blinded the minds of unbelievers, so they can't see the light of the Good News of Christ's glory—Christ, who is the image of God.
We don't preach ourselves. We preach Christ Jesus as Lord, and ourselves as your servants for Jesus' sake.
God once said, ‘Light will shine out of darkness.’ He has made his light shine in our hearts, giving us the light of knowing God's glory in the face of Jesus Christ.
But we carry this treasure in fragile clay jars, so it's clear that this extraordinary power comes from God and not from us.
We're pressured from every side, but not crushed; confused, but not without hope;
hunted down, but never abandoned; knocked down, but not destroyed.
We always carry in our bodies the death of Jesus, so that Jesus' life may also be revealed in our bodies.
While we live, we're always being handed over to death for Jesus' sake, so that his life may be revealed in our mortal bodies too.
So death is at work in us, but life is at work in you.
We have the same spirit of faith as the one who wrote, ‘I believed, so I spoke.’ We believe too, and that's why we speak.
We know that the one who raised the Lord Jesus will also raise us with Jesus and bring us with you into his presence.
All of this is for your benefit, so that grace may reach more and more people and overflow in thanksgiving to God's glory.
So we don't give up. Even though our physical body is wearing out, our inner self is being renewed every day.
Our present troubles are small and temporary, but they're producing for us an eternal glory that far outweighs them all.
We focus not on what can be seen, but on what can't be seen. What can be seen lasts only a short time, but what can't be seen lasts forever.
We know that if our earthly tent—this body we live in—is destroyed, God has a building ready for us: an eternal home in heaven, not made by human hands.
While we're in this tent, we groan and long to put on our heavenly home,
if indeed, when we put it on, we won't be found naked.
While we're in this tent, we groan under the burden. We don't want to be unclothed; we want to be clothed with our heavenly home, so that what is mortal may be swallowed up by life.
God is the one who prepared us for this very thing, and he gave us the Spirit as a guarantee.
So we're always confident. We know that as long as we live in the body, we're away from the Lord,
because we live by faith, not by what we see.
We're confident, I say, and would rather leave the body and be at home with the Lord.
So whether we're at home in the body or away from it, our goal is to please him.
We must all appear before Christ's judgment seat, so each person may receive what is due for what they did in the body, whether good or bad.
Because we know what it means to fear the Lord, we try to persuade people. God already knows us completely, and I hope you know us in your conscience too.
We're not trying to recommend ourselves to you again. We're giving you a reason to be proud of us, so you'll have an answer for those who boast about appearances instead of the heart.
If we seem out of our minds, it's for God; if we're clear-minded, it's for you.
Christ's love compels us, because we've concluded this: one died for everyone, and so everyone died.
He died for everyone so that those who live would no longer live for themselves, but for the one who died and was raised for them.
So from now on, we don't judge anyone from a merely human point of view. Even if we once viewed Christ that way, we don't anymore.
So if anyone is in Christ, they are a new creation. The old has passed away; look, the new has come!
All this comes from God, who reconciled us to himself through Christ and gave us the ministry of reconciliation:
God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself, no longer counting people's trespasses against them. And he entrusted us with the message of reconciliation.
So we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God were making his appeal through us. We beg you on Christ's behalf: be reconciled to God.
God made the one who knew no sin to be a sin offering for us, so that in him we could become God's righteousness.
As God's co-workers, we urge you not to receive his grace and then let it go to waste.
For God says, ‘At the right time I heard you; on the day of salvation I helped you.’ Look, now is the right time; now is the day of salvation.
We don't put any obstacle in anyone's way, so our ministry won't be discredited.
Instead, in every way we show that we're God's servants: through great endurance, troubles, hardships, and distress;
through beatings, imprisonments, riots, hard work, sleepless nights, and hunger;
through purity, knowledge, patience, kindness, the Holy Spirit, and sincere love;
through the true message, God's power, and the weapons of righteousness in both hands;
through honor and dishonor, bad reports and good reports; treated as impostors, yet telling the truth;
treated as unknown, yet well known; treated as dying, yet look—we live; punished, but not killed;
grieving, yet always joyful; poor, yet making many rich; having nothing, yet possessing everything.
We've spoken openly to you, Corinthians; our hearts are wide open.
We haven't held back our affection for you, but you've held back yours for us.
So, as my children, open your hearts to us too.
Don't bind yourselves together with unbelievers in a way that compromises your faith. What partnership is there between righteousness and lawlessness? What fellowship does light have with darkness?
What harmony is there between Christ and the devil? What does a believer share with an unbeliever?
What agreement can God's temple have with idols? We are the temple of the living God. As God said, ‘I will live with them and walk among them. I will be their God, and they will be my people.’
So the Lord says, ‘Come out from among them and be separate. Don't touch anything unclean, and I will welcome you.’
‘I will be a Father to you, and you will be my sons and daughters,’ says the Lord Almighty.
Dear friends, since we have these promises, let's cleanse ourselves from everything that contaminates body and spirit, bringing holiness to completion in reverence for God.
Make room for us in your hearts. We haven't wronged anyone, corrupted anyone, or taken advantage of anyone.
I'm not saying this to condemn you. I've already told you that you're in our hearts—to live together and to die together.
I can speak to you with great confidence. I'm very proud of you. I'm filled with comfort and overflowing with joy, even through all our troubles.
Even when we arrived in Macedonia, we had no rest. We were troubled in every way: conflicts on the outside, fears within.
But God, who comforts the downcast, comforted us through Titus' arrival,
and not only through his arrival. You also comforted him. He told us about your longing, your sorrow, and your concern for me, and that made me even more joyful.
Even though my letter made you sad, I don't regret writing it. I did regret it for a while, because I saw that it upset you, though only briefly.
Now I'm glad—not because you were made sad, but because your sorrow led you to turn back to God. You were grieved in a way that honors God, so you suffered no loss because of us.
Godly sorrow leads to a change of heart that brings salvation and leaves no regret. But worldly sorrow leads to death.

Look what this godly sorrow produced in you: real concern, a desire to clear things up, indignation, alarm, longing, commitment, and a desire for justice. In every way, you showed yourselves to be innocent in this matter.
So even though I wrote to you, it wasn't on behalf of the one who did wrong or the one who was wronged. I wrote so your concern for us would be clear before God.
That's why we've been comforted. And our comfort has been made even greater by the joy Titus felt, because you all refreshed his spirit.
If I had bragged to him about you, I wasn't put to shame. Just as everything we told you was true, our boasting to Titus proved true too.
His affection for you has grown even stronger as he remembers how you all obeyed and welcomed him with fear and trembling.
I'm glad I can be completely confident in you.
Brothers and sisters, we want you to know about the grace God has given the churches in Macedonia.
Even in a severe time of testing and deep poverty, they overflowed with joy and became remarkably generous.
I can confirm that they gave as much as they could—and even beyond what they could afford—entirely on their own.
They urgently begged us for the privilege of sharing in this service for God's people.
They did more than we expected: first they gave themselves to the Lord, and then, by God's will, they gave themselves to us too.
So we urged Titus, who had already started this work, to help you finish this act of grace as well.
Just as you excel in everything—in faith, speech, knowledge, eagerness, and love for us—excel in this grace of giving too.
I'm not commanding you to give. I'm showing you how eager others are, to test whether your love is genuine too.
You know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ: though he was rich, he became poor for your sake, so that through his poverty you could become rich.
Here's my advice: last year you were the first not only to act but also to want to do this.
So now finish what you started. Let your eagerness to do it be matched by completing it with what you have.
If you're eager to give, your gift is accepted according to what you have, not according to what you don't have.
We don't want others to have it easy while you are crushed.
We want fairness. Right now your surplus can meet their need, and later their surplus can meet yours. That's how fairness works.
As Scripture says, ‘The one who gathered a lot had nothing left over, and the one who gathered a little had no shortage.’
Thanks be to God, who put the same deep concern for you into Titus' heart.
He welcomed our appeal and was already so eager that he chose to come to you on his own.
We're sending along with him a brother whose work for the Good News is praised by all the churches.
The churches also appointed him to travel with us as we carry this gift, a service that honors the Lord and shows our eagerness to help.
We want to avoid any criticism about how we handle this generous gift.
We're taking care to do what is honorable, not only before the Lord but also before people.
We're also sending another brother who has often proved eager in many things. Now he is even more eager because he has great confidence in you.
As for Titus, he is my partner and co-worker in serving you. As for our brothers, they are representatives of the churches and bring honor to Christ.
So show these brothers proof of your love, and show the churches why we have been proud of you.
I don't really need to write to you about this service for God's people,
because I know you're ready to help. I've been boasting about you to the Macedonians, saying that Achaia has been ready since last year. Your enthusiasm has stirred up many of them.
Still, I'm sending the brothers so our boasting about you won't turn out to be empty talk. As I said, I want you to be ready.
Otherwise, if some Macedonians come with me and find you unprepared, we'd be embarrassed—let alone you—after being so confident in you.
So I thought it was necessary to urge the brothers to visit you ahead of us and prepare the generous gift you promised. Then it will be ready as a generous gift, not something given reluctantly.
Remember: whoever sows sparingly will also harvest sparingly, and whoever sows generously will also harvest generously.
Each of you should give what you've decided in your heart—not reluctantly or because someone pressures you. God loves a cheerful giver.
God can pour every kind of grace into your lives, so that you'll always have everything you need and plenty left over for every good work.
As Scripture says, ‘They freely give to the poor; their righteousness lasts forever.’
The one who supplies seed to the farmer and bread to eat will supply and multiply your seed for sowing and increase the harvest of your righteousness.
You'll be made rich in every way so you can be generous on every occasion, and your generosity will result in thanksgiving to God through us.
This service of giving does more than meet the needs of God's people; it also overflows in many thanksgivings to God.
Because of the way you serve, people will praise God for your obedience to the Good News of Christ and for your generous sharing with them and everyone else.
And as they pray for you, they'll long for you because of the extraordinary grace God has shown you.
Thanks be to God for his gift beyond words!
I, Paul, personally appeal to you by Christ's humility and gentleness. I may seem timid when I'm there with you but bold when I'm away.
I beg you not to make me show that same boldness in person when I come, as I plan to do toward some who think we live by human standards.
Even though we live in human bodies, we don't fight by human methods.
The weapons we fight with aren't human. They have God's power to tear down strongholds.
We tear down arguments and every proud obstacle raised against knowing God, and we take every thought captive to obey Christ.
Once your obedience is complete, we'll be ready to deal with every act of disobedience.
Look at what's right in front of you. If anyone is confident that they belong to Christ, they should remember that we belong to Christ just as much as they do.
Even if I boast a little too boldly about the authority the Lord gave us to build you up, not tear you down, I won't be ashamed of it.
I don't want it to seem like I'm trying to scare you with my letters.
Some say, ‘His letters are forceful and powerful, but in person he's unimpressive, and his speaking is nothing special.’
Those people should understand this: what we say by letter while away, we'll also do when we're there.

We don't dare put ourselves in the same class as those who recommend themselves. When they measure themselves by their own standards and compare themselves with one another, they show how little they understand.
We won't boast beyond our proper limits. We'll stay within the boundaries God assigned to us, which include you.
We aren't overstepping our limits as if we hadn't reached you. We were the first to bring you the Good News about Christ.
We don't boast about work others have done. We hope that as your faith grows, our work among you will expand within the area God assigned us,
so we can preach the Good News in regions beyond you, without boasting about work already done by someone else.
As Scripture says, ‘If you boast, boast about the Lord.’
The person who recommends themselves isn't the one who passes the test. The Lord's recommendation is what counts.
I wish you would put up with me in a little foolishness. Actually, you already are.
I'm jealous for you with a godly jealousy. I promised you to one husband, to present you to Christ as a pure bride.
But I'm afraid that, just as the serpent tricked Eve with his cunning, your minds may somehow be led away from sincere devotion to Christ.
If someone comes preaching a different Jesus from the one we preached, or you receive a different spirit or a different message of good news, you put up with it easily enough.
I don't think I'm in the least inferior to those so-called super-apostles.
Even if I'm not a trained speaker, I do have knowledge. We've made that clear to you in every way.
Did I sin by lowering myself so you could be lifted up, when I shared God's Good News with you free of charge?
I accepted support from other churches, in effect taking their wages so I could serve you.
When I was with you and needed help, I wasn't a burden to anyone. The brothers who came from Macedonia supplied what I needed. I kept from burdening you in every way, and I'll keep doing so.
As surely as Christ's truth is in me, no one in Achaia will stop me from boasting about this.
Why? Because I don't love you? God knows I do.
I'll keep doing what I've been doing so I can cut off the opportunity of those who want a chance to claim their work is just like ours.
People like that are false apostles, dishonest workers who disguise themselves as apostles of Christ.
And that's no surprise. Even Satan disguises himself as an angel of light.
So it's no surprise if his servants disguise themselves as servants of righteousness. Their end will match what they've done.
I'll say it again: don't think I'm foolish. But if you do, then accept me as a fool so I can brag a little too.
What I'm saying in this confident boasting isn't something the Lord would say; I'm speaking like a fool.
Since many people brag according to human standards, I'll brag too.
You put up with fools gladly because you think you're so wise!
You put up with anyone who enslaves you, takes advantage of you, exploits you, acts superior, or slaps you in the face.
To my shame, we were too weak for that! But if anyone dares to brag—and I'm speaking foolishly—I dare too.
Are they Hebrews? So am I. Are they Israelites? So am I. Are they Abraham's descendants? So am I.
Are they servants of Christ? (I'm out of my mind to talk like this.) I'm even more so: I've worked harder, been imprisoned more often, been beaten far more, and faced death again and again.
Five times I received from the Jews the forty lashes minus one.
Three times I was beaten with rods. Once I was stoned. Three times I was shipwrecked. I spent a night and a day adrift at sea.
I've been on many journeys and faced dangers from rivers, robbers, my own people, Gentiles, the city, the wilderness, the sea, and false believers.
I've worked hard and struggled, stayed awake many nights, gone hungry and thirsty, often gone without food, and been cold and without proper clothing.
Besides everything else, every day I carry the burden of concern for all the churches.
Who is weak without my feeling weak too? Who is led into sin without my burning with concern?
If I have to brag, I'll brag about the things that show my weakness.
God, the Father of the Lord Jesus, who is praised forever, knows I'm not lying.
In Damascus, the governor under King Aretas guarded the city to arrest me.
But I was lowered in a basket through a window in the wall, and escaped his hands.
There's nothing to gain from boasting, but I'll go on to visions and revelations from the Lord.
I know a man in Christ who was caught up to the third heaven fourteen years ago. Whether it was in his body or apart from his body, I don't know—God knows.
I know this man—whether in his body or apart from it, I don't know; God knows—
who was caught up into Paradise and heard things no one can express, things a person isn't allowed to repeat.
I'll boast about someone like that, but I won't boast about myself except in my weaknesses.
If I wanted to boast, I wouldn't be foolish, because I'd be telling the truth. But I won't, so no one will think more of me than what they see me do or hear me say.
To keep me from becoming conceited because of these extraordinary revelations, I was given a thorn in my flesh, a messenger of Satan to torment me and keep me from pride.
Three times I begged the Lord to take it away from me.
But he told me, ‘My grace is enough for you, because my power is made complete in weakness.’ So I'll gladly boast even more about my weaknesses, so Christ's power may rest on me.
That's why, for Christ's sake, I take pleasure in weaknesses, insults, hardships, persecutions, and difficulties. When I'm weak, then I'm strong.
I've been foolish to boast, but you pushed me to it. You should have commended me, because I'm in no way inferior to those so-called super-apostles, even though I am nothing.
The signs of a true apostle were done among you with great endurance—signs, wonders, and miracles.
How were you treated as less than the other churches, except that I wasn't a burden to you? Forgive me this wrong!

Look, I'm ready to visit you for a third time, and I still won't be a burden. I don't want what you own; I want you. Children shouldn't save up for their parents; parents should save up for their children.
I'll gladly spend everything I have and wear myself out for you. If I love you more, should you love me less?
Even so, I wasn't a burden to you. But some of you may say I was crafty and tricked you.
Did I take advantage of you through anyone I sent to you?
I urged Titus to go, and sent our brother with him. Did Titus take advantage of you? Didn't we act in the same spirit and follow the same steps?
Do you think we've been defending ourselves to you all this time? We speak in Christ before God. Dear friends, everything we do is to build you up.

I'm afraid that when I come I may not find you as I want, and you may not find me as you want. I'm afraid I'll find arguments, jealousy, anger, selfish ambition, slander, gossip, arrogance, and disorder.
I'm afraid that when I come again, my God will humble me before you, and I'll grieve over many who sinned before and haven't turned away from their impurity, sexual immorality, and reckless behavior.
This is my third visit to you. Scripture says, ‘Every matter must be confirmed by the testimony of two or three witnesses.’
I warned you when I was there the second time, and I'm warning you again now while I'm away: if I come again, I won't spare those who sinned before or anyone else.
You want proof that Christ speaks through me. He isn't weak toward you; he shows his power among you.
He was crucified in weakness, but he lives by God's power. We too are weak in him, but we'll live with him by God's power among you.
Examine yourselves to see whether you're living in the faith. Test yourselves. Don't you realize that Jesus Christ is in you?—unless you fail the test.
I hope you'll recognize that we haven't failed the test.
I pray to God that you won't do anything wrong—not so we can look successful, but so you'll do what is right, even if we seem to have failed.
We can't do anything against the truth; we can only work for the truth.
We're glad when we're weak and you're strong. We also pray that you'll be fully restored.
That's why I'm writing this while I'm away: so I won't have to be harsh when I come, using the authority the Lord gave me to build you up, not tear you down.
Finally, brothers and sisters: celebrate, be restored, encourage one another, agree with one another, and live in peace. Then the God of love and peace will be with you.
Greet one another with a holy kiss.
All God's people here send you their greetings.
May the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with you all. Amen.
